study_identification_part.si4_title: A 10-Year Longitudinal Study of Brain Cortical Thickness in People with FirstEpisode Psychosis Using Normative Models

nm2_1_modeling_method.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) normative models with age as a covariate and sex and scanner ID as batch effects; transfer learning used to adapt to new scanners before applying to longitudinal TOP data.
nm2_1_modeling_method.supporting_text: "To account for site and scanner effects, we used the Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) approach for normative modeling... using HBR with age as a covariate, and sex and scanner id as batch effects, to predict CT... We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners, by transferring the (hyper) parameters as informed priors for these new sites."

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness for 150 Destrieux atlas ROIs predicted by the normative models.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: "we estimated a normative model for each region of interest (ROI, n = 150) in the Freesurfer Destrieux atlas... to predict CT."
